The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. A producer fix, not a loosening. The three-line comment names the card number in source; AGENTS.md's no-tracker-number rule is for rules and runtime strings, and the codebase uses `[#NNNN]` code comments throughout, so no flag.

**Pinned-contract rows.** One row added to `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`: `(notify-written-address-channels.integration.test.ts, findOne, pinned: 1)`, placed where the gate's sort (file, then verb; `check-engine-double-contract.mjs:2627`) puts it, between `notify-organization-stamp` and `notify-zero-delivery-visibility`. **Would the A subset pass?** On the code read, yes: 47c6ea05 + e6878f86 + 011221d3 carry the written-out refusal, the new test's A to D cases, the ledger row, the `alert_exec` fix and a changeset whose text makes no claim about computed recipients. Its gate verdicts on its own head are not among this record's inputs (only the head's check-runs are), so an A record must be rendered on A's head once it exists. - `data/seed/index.ts` writes `showcase_invoice.owner` as `ada@example.com`, `linus@example.com`, `grace@example.com`; `PROVISIONED_USER_EMAILS` is `admin@objectos.ai`, `phone.demo@example.com`, `auditor.demo@example.com`.

So under B, approving a seeded invoice fails the run at `notify_cleared` with `(no user holds that address)` unless an operator has signed up as that owner. Before, it wrote the junk row and succeeded. Org-scoped when the run names its tenant; unscoped otherwise, which on a `single` install is the same set.
- *A dev boot really has that member.* `AuthPlugin.maybeSeedDevAdmin` runs on `kernel:ready` under `NODE_ENV === 'development'` (`isDevAdminSeedArmed`) and signs up `admin@objectos.ai` (`devSeedAdminEmail`'s default) through better-auth's own `signUpEmail`, then stamps `email_verified`. The INV-1010 path is the one the new test walks (below); the demo's own boot-time request behaves the same because it opens on a seeded `sent` invoice with the same owner population.
